property_summary: For any caller who is not the admin, owner remains unchanged after setOwner in the original, but changes in the buggy version.
For any caller, after a successful setOwner call, owner equals the new owner in the buggy version; in the original, only the admin can change it, so for non-admin callers, owner remains unchanged.
After a successful call to setOwner, the owner variable must equal the _owner parameter passed; the buggy version breaks this because it never assigns _owner to owner.

After any external setOwner call, the public owner variable must not change because admin is separate; the mutant changes admin instead, leaving owner untouched, violating the invariant that owner remains unchanged when setOwner is called by admin.

After a successful setOwner call by the admin, the owner variable must equal the argument passed; the mutant incorrectly updates admin instead, so owner remains unchanged and does not match the argument.
Only the contract admin can change the owner; the reference enforces this, but the bug allows any caller to set the owner.

The bug eliminates the onlyAdmin restriction, allowing any caller to change the owner; the property asserts that for any caller, the owner can only be set by the original admin, a rule the reference satisfies for all inputs and the mutant violates when a non-admin fuzzed address calls setOwner.
For any caller and any new owner address, setOwner does not revert if and only if the caller is the admin; the bug allows any caller to succeed, violating this rule when a non-admin calls it.
For any caller, setOwner succeeds only if the caller is the admin; the bug allows a non-admin to succeed.
any caller who is not the admin must not change the owner, but the mutant allows non-admin callers to change it
After any call to setOwner, the owner can only be changed if the caller is the original admin; the buggy version allows anyone who is already the owner to change owner again.

After any call to setOwner from a non-admin account that is not the current owner, the owner must remain unchanged; the buggy version allows any current owner to change the owner, so a non-admin who becomes owner can subsequently change the owner to a different account.

For any sequence of calls to setOwner, the final owner must be one of the addresses that have been admin in the system's lifetime; the buggy version allows the owner to be set by a non-admin that was never an admin.
setOwner always returns true on success in the reference, but the mutant returns false, so the return value for a valid admin call must be true.
